title: Fear

launchpad.outcome: Feel fear in a live trade, see what it pushes you toward, and separate a planned exit from a fearful one.

slides.kicker: Valid ICC · correct risk · correct entry
slides.title: Feel it first

checkpoints.prompt: Pullback. Nothing in your plan triggered. What do you do?
checkpoints.thought: “I DON’T WANT THIS TO TURN INTO A LOSER.”
checkpoints.after: Nothing in the plan triggered. The pullback stayed a pullback.

slides.intro: Your plan: SL −30, TP +60. No break-even rule. No partials.

ask.prompt: WHAT WAS FEAR TRYING TO MAKE YOU DO?

options.label: Protect unrealized profit by abandoning the management plan
options.why: That’s fear’s whole pitch: make the discomfort stop, even if it costs the plan.

options.label: Read new structure
options.feedback: Structure didn’t change. The candle color did.

options.label: Follow a break-even rule
options.feedback: There was no break-even rule. That’s why it would have been fear.

slides.title: They push you toward different things
slides.verdict: Same emotion family. Different behavior. Name which one is talking.

slides.title: What fear may produce
slides.note: May produce. Not always. Every exit isn’t fear, and every skipped trade isn’t either.

slides.title: Three early exits. Same price. Different reasons.

items.text: Her written plan: move to BE after a 1M close above +30. That close printed. She moved it.
Her early-intervention rule: exit on a 1M close below the 1H HL. That close printed. She exited.
items.why: New valid information her plan defined in advance.

items.text: “It felt like it might come back.” No rule triggered. She closed.
items.why: The plan didn’t change. Her comfort did.

slides.punch: Taking profit early isn’t automatically wrong. The question is WHY DID YOU EXIT?

lines: You can’t get certainty. You can follow the rules while you’re uncertain.

slides.quote: Fear doesn’t need to leave the room. It just doesn’t get to hold the mouse.

slides.prompt: What does fear look like in your trading decisions?
slides.modelAnswer: It looks like closing a planned trade to make the discomfort stop, moving to break even without a rule, or skipping a valid setup because the last one lost. I ask: management rule, new valid information, or fear?

takeaways: Fear of losing ≠ fear of being wrong.
remember: FEAR WANTS CERTAINTY. TRADING GIVES YOU PROBABILITIES + RULES.
